old_title: Ukraine-Russia war live: Nato jets scrambled in response to unidentified object
new_title: Ukraine war live: Kyiv 'has reclaimed more land than Moscow has captured in autumn'

Nato jets were scrambled in response to an unidentified flying object over Lithuania on Sunday morning, with residents in the central and northern parts of the country told to seek shelter.
The order to shelter lasted about an hour, and the government later said the object was likely a drone that entered from Poland.
Poland said it was also investigating the incident, but Nato jets were unable to visually identify the object due to cloudy conditions.
During the "red alert" Nato fighters were scrambled to the area and Kaunas airport, near Lithuania's second-largest city, was temporarily closed.
Earlier, Volodymyr Zelensky expressed hope that a bill of sanctions against Russia can be revived, calling on Kyiv's allies to "voice support" for the measures.
US president Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday that blocked a sweeping new sanctions package targeting the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause was in the "national interest". The sanctions were due to come into force today.
"This Act could have helped enormously - and still can! But it needs to actually work, and every voice in support of it matters," Zelensky wrote.
Starlink restrictions were planned, Zelensky says
Volodymyr Zelensky said that Kyiv was investigating sudden speed restrictions on Ukraine's use of Starshield, the military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service, which is the backbone of Ukraine's drone operations and communication.
The restrictions, imposed without warning early on Thursday, cut the internet data connection when a communication terminal moves faster than 160 kph (100 mph). The cap forced Ukrainian drones to fly slower than usual, making it easier for Russian weapons to target or evade them.
Zelensky said that there were no similar restrictions in European Union countries and that they apply only to Ukraine. "In other words, this is a planned operation," he said.
It was unclear who was responsible. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk said this week that the US government owns and controls the system, with decisions about its use resting with the US military and, ultimately, the president.
The Pentagon has not answered questions from The Associated Press about the restrictions.
Trump told reporters Friday that he did not order restrictions on the system. He also doubted that the disruption came from Musk.
On Saturday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the White House was not behind the reduction in service to SpaceX's Starlink.
Nato jets scrambled as Lithuania tells residents to go to shelters over flying object
Nato jets were scrambled in response to an unidentified flying object over Lithuania on Sunday morning, with residents in the central and northern parts of the country told to seek shelter.
The order to shelter lasted about an hour, and the government later said the object was likely a drone that entered from Poland.
Poland said it was also investigating the incident, but Nato jets were unable to visually identify the object due to cloudy conditions.
During the "red alert" Nato fighters were scrambled to the area and Kaunas airport, near Lithuania's second-largest city, was temporarily closed.
Northern neighbour Latvia briefly issued a "yellow" air warning in some regions bordering Lithuania.
Ukrainian drones have repeatedly entered Nato airspace in the Baltic region in recent months, with Kyiv saying they were steered off course by Russian signal jamming. Such incidents have stoked concerns that Russia's war on Ukraine could spill over Nato's borders.
Blaze at St Petersburg oil sites as Ukraine launches more than 1,000 drones at Russia
Ukrainian attacks set an oil export terminal ablaze in St Petersburg on Sunday, as Kyiv launched more than 1,000 drones across Russia in one of its largest ever aerial bombardments.
The attack comes amid deepening tensions between Ukraine and Washington, with Donald Trump criticising Kyiv for its strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.
One person was killed and five more were wounded in the attack, which sparked fires at both the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the city's Ruchi oil depot, said local governor Alexander Beglov.
A logistics centre belonging to Russian retailer Ozon and a data centre for local tech giant VK were also targeted, both companies confirmed.
Russia's defence ministry said its forces had destroyed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over 15 Russian regions, as well as the illegally-annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black Sea, overnight and on Sunday.
Zelensky working to arrange three way meeting with Putin and Trump
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky said the US was working to arrange a three-way meeting involving him, US president Donald Trump and Russian president Vladimir Putin, potentially in the Middle East, Europe or the United States.
Despite the latest executive order by Trump that has put fresh Russian sanctions on hold, bilateral talks between the US and Ukraine have not broken down.
Zelensky said Ukraine's lead negotiator, Rustem Umerov, had met on Friday with US presidential envoy Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law.
Rubio defends US agreement with Russia over diesel supplies
Marco Rubio has defended a separate US agreement with Russia to increase diesel supplies to global markets, aimed at easing fuel prices that have climbed amid the war with Iran and disruptions to energy supplies.
Under the agreement, Donald Trump said Russia initially would supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel to the US, followed by shipments in November and beyond.
"That diesel is going to be sold one way or the other," Rubio said. "The only difference is how much of it the United States was going to get."
Rubio said the diesel deal and sanctions waiver reflected the challenge of managing conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine that have disrupted global energy supplies.
"These conflicts around the world are starting to crash into each other," he said.
Rubio says Trump to take up to 60 days to weigh Russia sanctions
The day after waiving sanctions and tariffs related to Russian exports, US president Donald Trump said on Saturday he has yet to announce a final decision on the matter.
Secretary of state Marco Rubio said officials want more time to evaluate the situation.
Rubio said that the president will use up to 60 days to assess the economic impact of Russia-related sanctions and tariffs that he waived a day earlier.
"A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out," Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida.
The waiver comes just weeks before November's midterm elections, with Trump under pressure over high energy prices as war with Iran disrupts global oil supplies.
"I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the US economy," Rubio told reporters before boarding a plane for a trip to Uzbekistan.
Trump's deal with devil 'keeps getting dirtier'
"Beyond irresponsible," said senator Thom Tillis on social media, outraged about Donald Trump's decision to pause sanctions on Russia.
"What part of enforcing a law passed 86-11 by the Senate does the President and his advisers not understand?" Tillis said.
"It's unconscionable that this administration is capitulating to a Russian dictator who illegally invaded Ukraine.
"Republican senator John Cornyn of Texas said "Lindsey would be appalled," referring to the late senator Lindsey Graham, who worked tirelessly on the bill before he died this summer. The bill is known as the Lindsey Graham Russian Sanctions Act.
Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer of New York said in a statement that "by giving the Russian economy life support, Trump's deal with the devil keeps getting dirtier."
Senator Elizabeth Warren said Trump is "thumbing his nose" at Congress and "enabling Vladimir Putin to continue his war of aggression." She urged her colleagues to take action to reverse course.
Next steps uncertain with Congress out until after Election Day
Donald Trump's actions come as Ukraine is bracing for a stark winter confronting Russia's ongoing attacks on its energy infrastructure to heat homes and keep the lights on.
The next steps are highly uncertain with the House and Senate on recess until after Election Day. Trump had indicated he was waiving the sanctions indefinitely, citing national security concerns.
Later Saturday, Trump told reporters that they don't know what his decision is yet regarding sanctions in Russia, despite the executive order he signed Friday night.
"We'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out. But it's a very good decision, and it's going to be a decision that's good for the country, and I think good for the world," Trump said at a fundraising dinner at his Florida estate.
Secretary of state Marco Rubio, separately addressing reporters on Saturday before departing for Central Asia, suggested Trump would take 60 days to review the global and US economic impacts of imposing the proposed sanctions on Russia and other countries, in light of tariffs already in place.
Pointing to high energy prices and the Iran war, "we need that period of time to sort of study all this and figure out what the right combination is," he said.
Poland says it is verifying a possible violation of its airspace
Poland is verifying a possible violation of its airspace by an unidentified object, the army said on Sunday.
So far, there has been no confirmation of a violation of the airspace, the army said in a post on X.
The army said it had deployed a ground search-and-rescue team in the south of Lublin, which is conducting searches for the possible crash site of the object.
Zelensky hopes for revival of Russian sanctions
Ukraine's president expressed hope that sanctions that were supposed to take effect on Sunday targeting Russia's economy could be revived.
Volodymyr Zelensky described Donald Trump's move to put sanctions on hold as unfortunate, but did not directly criticise the US leader despite deepening tensions between Ukraine and Washington in recent days.
"A decision was unfortunately made in America to completely disregard the Lindsey Graham Act, which was supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end," Zelensky wrote in a statement on social media.
"This Act could have helped enormously - and still can! But it needs to actually work, and every voice in support of it matters."
He separately thanked Democrats and Republicans who supported the legislation, saying that blocking it would encourage Russia to continue killing and that limiting Ukraine's ability to retaliate would not bring peace.
"Nevertheless, we very much hope - and I personally hope - that the president of the United States of America will do everything possible to make (Russian president Vladimir) Putin stop the killing, stop the attacks on our energy infrastructure, and end this war," he said.
It took almost a year for Lindsey Graham to persuade Trump to agree to the Russian sanctions package.
It was designed to impose steep tariffs on countries that import large amounts of Russian oil and energy products and was promoted as a way to halt the flow of funds fuelling Putin's four-year war against Ukraine.

Ukraine has recaptured more territory this autumn than Russia has taken, Volodymyr Zelensky has said as his forces pushed further into occupied areas of Donetsk.
In a statement on social media, the Ukrainian president said that Kyiv was seeing "results on the front" as well as stepping up its long-range drone campaign behind enemy lines in Russia.
"The trend this year continues," Zelensky said. "Since the start of fall, our warriors have liberated more territory than the Russians have managed to capture. The same was true at other points this year."
Ukrainian generals say that Operation Vivaldi had seen the return of liberation and return of 16 settlements and 277 square kilometres to Ukraine.
Elsewhere, Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones against Russia and set an oil terminal ablaze in St Petersburg after the US resumed intelligence sharing with Kyiv.
The attacks, which sparked fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the city's Ruchi oil depot, killed one person and injured five.
Russia, in turn, unleashed strikes on Ukraine's energy, oil, and gas sectors, carrying out at least 76 times over the last 24 hours.
Ukraine has reclaimed more territory than Russia has captured, says Zelensky
Ukraine has recaptured more territory this autumn than Russia has taken, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
In a statement on social media, the Ukrainian president said that Kyiv was seeing "results on the front" as well as stepping up its long-range drone campaign behind enemy lines in Russia.
"The trend this year continues," Zelensky said. "Since the start of fall, our warriors have liberated more territory than the Russians have managed to capture. The same was true at other points this year."
Rubio says Ukraine and Russia should be focused on ending the war
US secretary of state Marco Rubio said Ukraine and Russia should focus on ending their four-year war, warning of the risk of escalation into neighbouring countries.
Asked about a possible meeting between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, Rubio said the summit had not been finalised but reiterated Trump's desire to end the conflict.
"There's been talks of a meeting. I don't know whether it's been finalised, but the president has been clear. He'd like the war in Ukraine and Russia to end."
"We see nothing good coming from this war," Rubio said.
"We see a lot of downside to it, including the very real risk of escalation and spread of this thing... into another country because of a failed sabotage attack, because of drones that are hit with electronic warfare and they wander into a neighbouring country."
Putin proposes summit with Trump and Xi - report
Russian president Vladimir Putin has proposed a summit next month with US president Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping to negotiate an end to the four-year Ukraine conflict that would favour Moscow, the Wall Street Journal said.
Citing a former Russian intelligence officer, the paper said on Sunday that Putin's suggestion came in a 9 October telephone call with Trump that also yielded a deal for the US to buy Russian diesel and facilitate its sale on the global market.
Bessent warns Zelensky to 'be very careful' about claims US is throttling Starlink
US treasury secretary Scott Bessent warned Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky to "be very careful" after he suggested Washington was responsible for restrictions on Ukraine's military Starlink system, which has affected its drone operations.
Bessent called the accusation "very reckless", saying Donald Trump and secretary of state Marco Rubio had denied ordering the restrictions.
However, Elon Musk said Starshield's limits - Starshield is the military and government-controlled version of the commercial Starlink - were ultimately decided by the US government, while Reuters reported that the White House had ordered the restrictions.
Trump has denied responsibility.
"President [Donald] Trump and Secretary [Marco] Rubio have categorically said that no one under the Trump administration did that, and I think it is very reckless for President Zelenskyy to make such a charge," Bessent said.
"President Zelenskyy should be very careful about making statements like this that aren't true," he added.
Ukraine has retaken more territory than Russia captured this fall, Zelensky claims
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine had recaptured more territory than Russia had seized since the start of autumn.
Under "Operation Vivaldi", Ukrainian forces reportedly reclaimed 277sq km and 16 settlements in Donetsk Oblast, The Kyiv Independent reported.
"We are seeing results on the front," Zelensky said.
"Since the start of fall, our warriors have liberated more territory than the Russians have managed to capture. The same was true at other points this year."
The Institute for the Study of War, a conflict monitor based in the US, said the Russian military claims of advances were "greatly exaggerated" and did not reflect battlefield realities.
Ukraine will 'not prevail' if Trump sides with Russia, Zelensky says
Blaze at St Petersburg oil sites as Kyiv launches more than 1,000 drones at Russia
Ukrainian attacks set an oil export terminal ablaze in St Petersburg on Sunday, as Kyiv launched more than 1,000 drones across Russia in one of its largest ever aerial bombardments.
The attack comes amid deepening tensions between Ukraine and Washington, with US president Donald Trump criticising Kyiv for its strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.
One person was killed and five more were wounded in the attack, which sparked fires at both the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the city's Ruchi oil depot, said local Gov. Alexander Beglov.
A logistics centre belonging to Russian retailer Ozon and a data centre for local tech giant VK were also targeted, both companies confirmed.
Zelensky blames US for intentionally throttling Starlink satellite internet access
Volodymyr Zelensky blamed the US on Sunday for intentionally throttling its Starlink satellite internet access.
However, he also thanked the Trump administration for resuming intelligence sharing between the two countries.
In an interview on NBC, Zelensky said that the "intelligence" was "blocked for some period of time. And then it was deblocked by the American side. We are very thankful for this. Now it works."
He added: "Only [the] United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. And we didn't get it during ballistic attacks during three days."
He also said that SpaceX limited the speed at which Starlink terminals worked in Ukraine, hampering drone operations on the frontlines as well as some air defence missions.
"It was a message from [the] American government to limit the speed," he said. "And technically, SpaceX did it."
Trump accuses Zelensky of not wanting to end war
Donald Trump has accused Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky of not wanting to end the war with Russia, as tensions between Washington and Kyiv continue over the US administration's approach to Moscow.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump defended his decision to waive some sanctions on Russia, saying he wanted to avoid undermining ongoing peace negotiations.
"My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don't want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table," he wrote.
"Zelensky doesn't care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him ... he doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did," he added.
Zelensky, meanwhile, thanked the Trump administration for resuming intelligence-sharing between the two countries, while maintaining that the US had deliberately restricted Ukraine's access to Starlink satellite internet services to send a "message" to Kyiv.
Putin proposes summit with Trump and Xi - report
Russian president Vladimir Putin has proposed a summit next month with US president Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping to negotiate an end to the four-year Ukraine conflict that would favour Moscow, the Wall Street Journal said.
Citing a former Russian intelligence officer, the paper said on Sunday that Putin's suggestion came in a 9 October telephone call with Trump that also yielded a deal for the US to buy Russian diesel and facilitate its sale on the global market.
